newsitem.title: GERMANY: POLICE IN DARK IN NEW NESTLE BLACKMAIL BID.
newsitem.headline: POLICE IN DARK IN NEW NESTLE BLACKMAIL BID.

text.p: German police said Wednesday they have no clue to the identity of an extortionist who claims to have poisoned Nestle food products in over 50 grocery stores in 14 cities.

The company's German unit, Deutsche Thomy GmbH, has been the target of blackmail efforts for the past 12 months and received fresh demands in a letter on Monday warning that its food products had been poisoned.

Authorities did not inform the public until Tuesday evening about the letter, the latest in a series of blackmail attempts that only became public in April after poisoned food was found in stores in two German cities.
After the latest blackmail attempt, police said they still did not know whether the extortion plot was the act of an individual or a group.
"We have no clues," Franz Winkler, a spokesman for the police in Frankfurt, told Reuters. "The situation has not changed since yesterday evening."

The Aug. 11 letter also claimed that four weeks ago, 23 packages of poisoned Nestle products had been left in public areas such as parks, street cars, buses, train stations and phone booths, police said.
The blackmailer claimed to have left packages in cities such as Berlin, Bremen, Chemnitz, Dortmund, Dresden, Frankfurt, Hamburg, Cologne, Munich, Nuremberg, Regensburg and Stuttgart, police said.

The new announcement sparked a nationwide alert and some 10,000 people flooded the police with phone calls and another 60,000 called -- but were unable to get through -- after an emergency number was broadcast to the public on Tuesday.
German television reports showed pictures of rows of empty shelves in supermarkets after Nestle and Thomy products, such as mustard and mayonnaise, had been removed.
Police declined to say how much money was being demanded, but ZDF public television, citing anonymous sources, said blackmailers were insisting on $15 million in uncut diamonds.
The latest effort followed two earlier attempts to blackmail the company, in August 1996 and then in April.
Police said they believed the same blackmailer was responsible in each case.
